newsitem.title: USA: US spot resids steady to up, LSFO gains with crude.
newsitem.headline: US spot resids steady to up, LSFO gains with crude.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices were unchanged to up slightly on Friday in thin trade, with a sharp rally in crude and some utility buying interest helping low sulphur grades, industry sources said.

"With crude and natgas up, everything is talked better, but it's still mostly talk. I don't see any great demand," said one cash trader, noting some light low sulphur interest for utility requirements, mostly in early May.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent edged up slightly to $15.25 a barrel, with May one percent paper done at $15.30, about 15 cents firmer, traders said.
NYH June one percent paper also was talked slightly higher at $15.45-60, with Q3 pegged at $15.60-16.00.
While stronger crude may have put a temporary floor under resid, traders said the slack demand shoulder season ahead promised little upside near-term.
NYH 0.3 percent low pour and high pour also scored modest gains Friday to $18.25 and $16.25, respectively.
High sulphurs in New York held steady, traders said.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices again were stable, with one percent still at $15.00-25 and three percent at $13.50.

New York city gate weekend gas prices slipped a few cents Friday to about the $2.40/mmBtu level, or $15.12 a barrel equivalent. Gas at Henry Hub, the NYMEX delivery point, was up slightly to about $2.09/mmBtu, or $13.17 a barrel.
